label: thm:ew-triplet-charge-spin-from-involution
title: Sector label and charge of the electroweak triplet computed through the spin involution
html:
Conditional on the electroweak sector-selection postulate. Let R be a field with \tfrac{1}{2} \in R, and let \sigma be the spin involution, acting on the two-dimensional sym/alt block of the electroweak Hoefsmit cells as the swap \sigma(x, y) = (y, x). Assume the sector-selection postulate: each electroweak carrier c lies in the \sigma-even sector A_+ or the \sigma-odd sector A_-, with H \in A_+ (the self-dual Higgs carrier) and W^\pm, Z \in A_-; c has carrier eigenvalue a_c = q^{2k} \in R^\times with a_c^2 \neq 1; and a_{W^-} = a_{W^+}^{-1}, so that W^- carries the \sigma-image of W^+. Let v_c be the \sigma-even projection of (a_c, a_c^{-1}) if c \in A_+ and its \sigma-odd projection if c \in A_-. Define the sector label 2s(c) = 0 if \sigma v_c = v_c and 2s(c) = 2 otherwise, and the charge Q(c) = \mathrm{skew}(v_c), where \mathrm{skew}(x, y) = x - y. Then

  2s(H) = 0, \qquad 2s(W^\pm) = 2s(Z) = 2,
  Q(H) = 0, \qquad Q(W^+) \neq 0, \qquad Q(W^-) = -Q(W^+).

Both the sector label and the charge are computed from the action of \sigma on the sector vectors v_c.

The label 2s is a two-valued sector label of the model, named "spin" because A_+ is read as scalar and A_- as vector; it is not a computation of Lorentz spin. The sectors A_\pm are the two one-dimensional \mathbb{Z}/2-sectors of \sigma, not spin multiplets.

The theorem does not assign isospin. The paper's table 2T_3(W^\pm) = \pm 1, 2T_3(Z) = 2T_3(H) = 0 (so T_3(W^\pm) = \pm\tfrac12, the doublet values of the spin involution, not the triplet values \pm 1) is recorded, not derived from \sigma, and it is not a function of Q of the form \lambda Q + \mu: the row H forces \mu = 0, the row Z forces \lambda = 0 because Q(Z) \neq 0, and the row W^+ then fails. The normalised charge Q(c)/Q(W^+) takes the values 1, -1, 0 on W^+, W^-, H and a nonzero value on Z. The spin-involution rule, 2T_3 = 0 on A_+ and 2T_3 = \pm 1 on A_-, with the sign read as the sign of Q over an ordered field with a_{W^+}, a_Z > 1, gives 2T_3(H) = 0, 2T_3(W^\pm) = \pm 1 and 2T_3(Z) = 1. Each reading agrees with the table except at Z. In particular T_3(H) = 0 is a consequence of H \in A_+ under that rule, not an input of this theorem.

The \sigma-parity alone gives Q(Z) \neq 0, since Z \in A_-. Weinberg mixing does not repair this for a linear charge. Write Z = cW^3 - sB and \gamma = sW^3 + cB with c^2 + s^2 = 1, and extend Q linearly from x = Q(W^3) and y = Q(B). Then Q(Z)^2 + Q(\gamma)^2 = x^2 + y^2, so Q(Z) = Q(\gamma) = 0 holds only if x = y = 0. If W^3 and B are \sigma-odd sector vectors with non-degenerate eigenvalues, as the \sigma_5^8 grading places B, then x \neq 0 and no angle makes both Z and \gamma neutral.

Interpretation. In the Standard Model W^3 and B both carry zero electric charge, and that is why Z and \gamma are both neutral; the rotation does not create neutrality. The model's T_3(H) = 0 differs from the Standard Model, where the neutral component of the Higgs doublet has T_3 = -\tfrac{1}{2}.
